what: the v1_10_1 selector — pixel's second colour index, the one drawing change in 0.3.0
note: `test: null` — the whole suite — because the rule is decided in
avatar.dart and observed in pixel.dart, two parity files and the
cross-selector group in v1_10_1_parity_test.dart; a narrowed run would
report survivors for mutations another file kills.
Group A is the version→drawing decision. A-1 collapses the eras the way
a reader 'tidying' the switch would; A-2 and A-3 swap or half-swap the
index rule. All three render a perfectly plausible avatar — only a
comparison against the other selector, or against upstream's measured
values, can tell.
Group B is the arithmetic itself in pixel.dart. B-1 shifts the divisor
one further (i + 2): every tile still gets a colour from the palette, so
no structural assertion can see it — only the measured value list. B-2
collapses the new era onto the old inside the builder, below the
dispatch, which is the layer A-1 cannot reach.
Group C is the title seam extended to the new selector: the shared
`v1_7_0 || v1_10_1` arm split so that only v1_10_1 defaults the title
on. The output is well-formed and correct for v1_7_0, so only a
v1_10_1-side default render can catch it.
One mutation is verified BY HAND rather than by a case here, because it
needs two simultaneous edits and cases are single substitutions: rename
pixel's mask id AND its reference only when colourIndex is
loopIndexPlusOne. The #45 refuting lens found it surviving the whole
suite (every byte gate normalises ids; goldens are id-blind; pixel's
builder is the only one that receives version information). It now dies
on `the raw literals this port emits on the v1_10_1 path` in
v1_10_1_parity_test.dart — applied, watched red (exactly that test),
reverted, 2026-08-14.
This file's first run (2026-08-14) was taken over a RED baseline — the
README gates were deliberately still failing — so its '7/7 killed' was
unfalsifiable; run.mjs now refuses that with BASELINE RED. Re-run after
the docs land. A known survivor if anyone adds it: replacing
`jsMod(numFromName, i + 1)` with `numFromName % (i + 1)` is a true
equivalence (the hash is non-negative), not a gap — do not add a case
that cannot die.
